areycruzer opened issue #101: Startup exits with raw Os {NotFound}/{IsADirectory} when the auth-token file is missing or a directory — request: name the attempted path in the error
With `CLOUD_PROVIDER=local`, `LOCAL_PATH=/data/graph`, image `ghcr.io/hydra-db/hydradb@sha256:db78309a233be54662db29744047e985a39b51c45a270d1a1f47c31a62cdb709` (source commit `02a40025`), a fresh empty store bootstraps cleanly on macOS/Docker Desktop but on a GitHub `ubuntu-latest` runner the node starts, reaches placement state `fresh`, then exits:

```
Error: Os { code: 21, kind: IsADirectory, message: "Is a directory" }
```

Observed while narrowing (each a separate CI run):
- `LOCAL_PATH` absent → fails canonicalize: `UnableToCanonicalize { path: "/data/graph" ... NotFound }` — so the path must pre-exist;
- `LOCAL_PATH` pre-created (dir, owned by uid 10001 or mode 777) → placement reaches `fresh`, then `IsADirectory`;
- the same compose file and image bootstrap from an empty dir without issue on macOS/Docker Desktop, creating `graph/` and `cache/` subtrees itself.

Public repro: the `engine` job of https://github.com/areycruzer/substrate-friction/blob/main/.github/workflows/hydra-verify.yml (failing runs are public in that repo's Actions history; the job is `continue-on-error` and documents this issue as the cause).

areycruzer commented: Sharper evidence, from local bisection (all with the digest-pinned image `db78309a…`, full env parity via a compose override that swaps only the mount):

| Filesystem under `/data` | Result |
|---|---|
| macOS Docker Desktop bind mount (VirtioFS) | boots, creates `graph/graph/...` + `cache/...` itself |
| Docker **named volume** (ext4 inside the same Linux VM) | placement reaches `fresh`, then `Error: Os { code: 2, kind: NotFound }` |
| **Container overlayfs** (`LOCAL_PATH=/tmp/store/graph`, no volume at all) | same `NotFound` |
| GitHub runner bind mount (original report) | `IsADirectory` / `NotFound` variants |

Two additional data points:
- The failing boots write **nothing** into the store — the tree is exactly what was pre-seeded, so the crash is on a read/metadata op, not a failed write.
- Pre-seeding the complete directory tree that a successful macOS boot creates (`graph/graph/data/{namespaces,_graph_nodes,_graph_scopes}` + `cache/scopes/default/graphs`, owned by 10001) does **not** help — same `NotFound`.

areycruzer commented: **Correction — my earlier conclusion was wrong, and strace found the real cause.**

The engine cold-starts **fine** on every Linux filesystem I previously reported as failing. The last file syscall before every death was:

```
openat(AT_FDCWD, "/var/run/secrets/slatedb-graph/auth-token", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC) = -1 ENOENT
```

Root cause, entirely on my side:
- Our compose mounts `./secrets/token:/run/secrets/token:ro` with `GRAPH_AUTH_TOKEN_FILE` — and `secrets/` is **gitignored**, so a CI checkout doesn't have it. Docker bind-mounts the missing host path as an empty **directory**, and the engine dies reading its token with `IsADirectory`.
- My named-volume repro used a compose override with `volumes: !override`, which **stripped the secrets mount** — hence `NotFound` at the fallback secrets path.
- VirtioFS was never the variable; macOS "worked" because the file exists locally.

With the token file provisioned, the same digest boots and serves on ext4 named volumes, overlayfs, and the GitHub runner — our CI engine job (boot → Bolt round trip → wipe → engine test suite) is now green: https://github.com/areycruzer/substrate-friction/actions/workflows/hydra-verify.yml
